title: Configuration overlays lose explicit nulls and retain removed list entries
description: A deployment preview applies several configuration layers, then reports exactly which setting paths changed. The current implementation confuses an explicit null value with removal, extends lists that should be replaced, and reports parent objects instead of precise nested changes. Repair the existing merge_config API and its helpers together.

requirements.text: Apply layers from left to right. Objects merge recursively; scalars and lists replace existing values; a list never appends to an earlier list. An object replacing a scalar begins from an empty object.

Only the exact patch object {"$delete": true} deletes a key. An explicit null is ordinary data. Deleting an absent key is a no-op; deletion directives are allowed only as nested patch values, not as a whole layer, inside lists, or in the base configuration.

Return {config, changed}. changed is the lexically ordered list of dotted paths whose final value differs from base. Recurse when both values are objects; report an added/deleted whole object at its parent path. List replacement is one path, and type changes count (true differs from 1). Reverted changes disappear.

Validate all layers before merging. Base and each layer must be objects; layers must be a list. Keys must be nonempty strings without dots and must not start with $. Values may be objects, lists, null, strings, plain integers or booleans. Invalid input raises ValueError.
Never mutate base, layers, or any nested lists and objects, including when validation fails.
